main_text.head: CONCIO XLII.
Matth. 9.

p.i: T[?]unc adeunt eum discipuli Ioannis dicentes: Quam ob causam nos & Pharisæi ieiunamus plerunque, discipuli vero tui non ieiunant? Et dixit illis Iesus: Num possunt filij sponsi lugere, quandiu cum illis est sponsus? Venient autem dies, quum tolletur ab eis sponsus, & tunc ieiunabunt. Nullus immittit assumentum panni rudis in vestem veteri: aufert enim supplementum illius a vestimento, & peior ruptura fit. Neque mittunt vinum nouum in vtres veteres, alioqui rumpuntur vtres, & vinum effunditur, & vtres perëunt. Sed mittunt vinum nouum in vtres nouos, & vtraque simul seruantur.

main_text.p: ı Quæstio hic proponitur Christo (qui cum peccatoribus comederat) de ieiunio, quæ duo habet. vnum, quam ob causam discipuli Ioannis & Pharisæi crebrò ieiunent: alterum, cur discipuli sui (quos tamen ipse conetur docere viam meliorem & perfectiorem ad vitam æternam) non ieiunent, sed vt Lucas habet cap. 5. edant & bibant? In qua expostulatione multa notanda sunt. Primò:

page.notes: The woodcut initial at the start of the first paragraph is not legible; the first letter is a guess (T) and marked [?]. The running head "NVPTIALES." and the page number "169" are read from a slightly faded print. The Scripture passage appears to be wholly italic; the line "difcipuli vero tui non ieiunant?" may be roman, but I could not separate it with certainty. The "ı" before "Quæstio" is a small numeral mark, transcribed as printed. Long s has been normalised to s; u/v and i/j to the modern rule; "vnum" and "vt" have been changed to "unum" and "ut". Printing errors left as printed: "ieiunent,fed" (missing space) is written as "ieiunent, sed" with the space supplied.
